speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe when the fever and seizure started, and when the rash first appeared? Also, have you traveled recently or been in contact with anyone who was sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Does the rash fade when you press a glass against it, and has the infant returned to their normal activity level and appetite since the fever resolved?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The rash is likely blanching, and the infant appears well and back to normal activity. Given the high fever, febrile seizure, and subsequent rash in a vaccinated infant, this presentation is classic for Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum).

DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)
